title: Staff Backend Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also <a href="https://monzo.com/savings">save</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/investments">invest </a>and <a href="https://monzo.com/pensions">combine their pensions</a> with us. </p> <p>With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!</p> <p>We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.</p> <hr> <p> </p></div><p>📍London / UK Remote | 💰 <a href="https://monzo.com/documents/engineering-progression-framework-v4-0.pdf">Staff Backend Engineer (L60)</a> £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity + <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/">Benefits</a> | <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/technology">Technology</a> - Engineering  </p> <p><strong>About our Engineering Teams:</strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We have around 650 engineers out of roughly 5,500 people in total - and we have big ambitions. There are many interesting challenges ahead, and we're happy for people to move between teams or to specialise, whatever you prefer. As an engineer here you'd be able to work directly with anyone across the company, and we run regular knowledge-sharing sessions so you’ll learn heaps about everything from how banks work to effective communication.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We contribute to </span><a href="https://github.com/monzo"><strong>open source software</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> as much as possible. Our </span><a href="https://monzo.com/blog/technology"><strong>blog</strong></a><strong> </strong><span style="font-weight: 400;">is a good place to learn even more about what we do!</span></p> <p><strong>What you’ll be working on: </strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We rely heavily on the following tools and technologies:</span></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="http://golang.org/"><strong>Go</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> to write our application code (there’s an excellent interactive Go tutorial </span><a href="https://tour.golang.org/welcome/1"><strong>here</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">)</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="http://cassandra.apache.org/"><strong>Cassandra</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for most persistent data storage</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="http://kafka.apache.org/"><strong>Kafka</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for our asynchronous message queue</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://www.envoyproxy.io/"><strong>Envoy Proxy</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for RPC</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="http://kubernetes.io/"><strong>Kubernetes</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> and </span><a href="https://www.docker.com/"><strong>Docker</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> to schedule and run our services </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="http://aws.amazon.com/"><strong>AWS</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for most of our infrastructure</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><a href="https://facebook.github.io/react/"><strong>React</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for internal web dashboards</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">We also have two physical datacenter sites with actual cables to connect to various third parties</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>Your day-to-day   </strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This role is all about collaborating across disciplines to test hypotheses and make a difference to customers. As a product backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more! </span></p> <p>Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). Our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront - from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space.</p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles.</span></p> <p><strong>How we work 💻</strong></p> <p><strong>Locations & Flexible Working: </strong></p> <p>Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. </p> <p>We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs. ✨</p> <p>Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️. Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.</p> <p><strong>Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life:</strong></p> <p>At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance. </p> <p>You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency. 🕒✨</p> <p>If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance.</p> <p><strong>Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼</strong></p> <p><strong>You should apply if:</strong></p> <ul> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you have strong experience working on the backend of a technology product</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you have some experience with strongly-typed languages (Go, Java, C, Scala etc.).</span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">you think you’d enjoy the kind of work we’re doing</span></li> </ul> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We're on the look out for L60 Engineers at the moment, you can read more in our<a href="https://monzo.com/documents/engineering-progression-framework-v4-1.pdf"> Engineering Progression Framework</a> we are also hiring on L40 & L50, our interview process will determine your levelling. </span></p> <p><strong>The Interview Process:</strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Our interview process involves three main stages: </span></p> <ol> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Initial Call </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Take home task or pair coding exercise </span></li> <li style="font-weight: 400;"><span style="font-weight: 400;">Final interview including a system design and a behavioural interview </span></li> </ol> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Our average process takes around 2-3 weeks but we will always work around your availability. </span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">One of our engineers has written a detailed blog on their experience through this process, for extra details, hints and tips please see </span><a href="https://monzo.com/blog/2022/03/23/demystifying-the-backend-engineering-interview-process"><strong>here</strong></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">.<br><em>We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. </em><u><em><span><a href="https://monzo.com/blog/the-ultimate-guide-on-using-ai-to-ace-an-interview-at-monzo" target="_blank">You can read them here.</a></span></em></u><br></span></p> <p><strong>What’s in it for you:</strong></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 400;">💰 £130,000 - £170,000 + Equity</span></p> title: Marketing Automation Engineer
description: <h1>Growth at Private Equity Insights</h1> <p>Are you looking to work in an exceptional entrepreneurial team with ambitious, motivated and extremely driven people? And do you want real ownership from your first week? If so, now is the time to apply for the Growth role at Private Equity Insights.</p> <p>The mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors.</p> <p>You will work in sprints and get fast execution under your skin. AI has completely changed the game: You will learn to deploy it to outperform a marketing team of 20+ people, while also learning the fundamentals of copywriting that makes elite investors act, get it to the right investor at a meaningful frequency and deploy what works across every marketing channel.</p> <p>If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.</p> <h2><strong>Why Private Equity Insights</strong></h2> <p>Private Equity Insights is the world’s largest Private Equity community with 1m PE professionals, delivering impact through 12 global PE conferences with thousands of the world’s best investors and operators such as Blackstone, BlackRock, Apollo, Carlyle, CVC, KKR, and many more.</p> <p>Private Equity Insights is part of United Media (<a href="https://www.united-media.com/">https://www.united-media.com/</a>) which focuses on building large-scale industry media and conferences products in sectors such as insurance, finance, retail, etc. As of today, we have organically launched 5 media companies and exited 1.</p> <h2><strong>What we offer you</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Master the highest bar in the world.</strong> Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.</li> <li><strong>Unlimited growth potential. </strong>You will get responsibility before you feel ready. That is how you grow fast. We strongly believe in and have a track record of promoting internally. You can expect coaching and development from leaders, peers and experts.</li> <li><strong>Skills that compound for life.</strong> Fast execution, copywriting, pricing, conversion optimisation, structured problem solving, and the ability to create impact anywhere in the business at scale.</li> <li><strong>Ownership from the very start.</strong> You own outcomes, not tasks. We agree the goal, and you find the way.</li> <li><strong>Travel opportunity.</strong> You will be joining our 10+ conferences.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you will do</strong></h2> <p>Responsibilities in this job will vary, however, feed into the mission: build the world's largest network for private equity investors. They will be mostly centered around the following:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Build the audience.</strong> Identify, target, and convert every fund into our community, and make sure each one receives the right message, at the right time, and never one too many.</li> <li><strong>Own marketing channels that drive revenue. </strong>Through existing and new marketing channels, you execute activities that ultimately will drive revenue</li> <li><strong>Write copy that persuades.</strong> Every email, landing page and post. Become the best copywriter and leverage it at scale with AI.</li> <li><strong>Sprint, test, implement.</strong> Measure the impact of all experiments you run, test offers, copy, prices and pages until the numbers move.</li> <li><strong>Build systems, not one-offs.</strong> Anything you do twice becomes a playbook or an AI workflow, so the next win takes less effort than the last.</li> <li><strong>Do whatever it takes to win.</strong> Some days that means designing an AI workflow. Some days it means checking investors in at the registration desk at 7am. Nobody here is too good for the work that deliver value for investors and fund managers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What we expect from you</strong></h2> <ul> <li>1 to 3 years of experience</li> <li>Min. a bachelor or master degree with great results</li> <li>A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.</li> <li>Strong work ethic with a sense of urgency</li> <li>Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do</li> <li>Proactive approach and sense of ownership/responsibility of everything you do</li> <li>A humble approach and share our passion for building companies and developing people</li> <li>Interested in continuous learning and proactively searching for ways to optimise</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Practical details</strong></h2> <p>Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.</p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

You combine solid technical expertise with a growing ability to connect architecture decisions to customer outcomes.</p> <p><strong>The Impact You Will Have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Guide enterprise customers through the full lifecycle of Databricks on their cloud platform, including platform administration from initial architectural design to production deployment</li> <li>Architect secure, scalable enterprise deployments that satisfy complex cloud networking (virtual networks, private connectivity), identity (cloud IAM and enterprise identity providers), and security compliance standards. </li> <li>Advise customers on securing AI features (model boundaries, partner-hosted models, data residency, audit and evidence) and help them through security reviews to enable them.</li> <li>Run cross-account programmes to unblock adoption: track status, escalate, and report to leadership, Product and Security.</li> <li>Act as a technical specialist in core areas such as cloud infrastructure, infrastructure-as-code (IaC), cloud networking, and identity management</li> <li>Support technical wins in competitive scenarios by demonstrating Databricks' differentiation through custom-built solutions</li> <li>Collaborate with cross-functional resources (DSAs, SAs, FDE, Partners) to contribute to solutions for complex customer needs</li> <li>Operate with growing autonomy on well-scoped engagements, with guidance from senior architects on the most complex designs</li> <li>Influence product direction by providing structured feedback on customer requirements and competitive gaps</li> </ul> <p><strong>What We Look For</strong></p> <ul> <li>4+ years in solutions architecture, technical pre-sales, or a Network architecture hands-on technical role</li> <li>Strong expertise across the following areas:</li> <ul> <li>Security & Identity: Cloud security controls, platform/network/data security, encryption, vulnerability management, compliance, and identity protocols. This includes cloud-native IAM (AWS IAM, Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD, Google Cloud IAM), enterprise identity services (AWS IAM Identity Center, Entra ID, Google Cloud Identity), and federation standards (SCIM, OAuth, SAML, OIDC). Experience with EMEA regulatory frameworks (GDPR, DORA, FCA/PRA, EU AI Act) and turning them into technical controls and evidence.</li> <li>Lead technical answers to customer security, vendor-risk and AI-readiness questionnaires, working with Trust and Security.</li> <li>Networking & Deployments: Enterprise cloud networking (VPC/VNet design and peering, dedicated interconnects such as AWS Direct Connect / Azure ExpressRoute / Google Cloud Interconnect, and private connectivity such as AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Link / GCP Private Service Connect), network routing, performance optimisation, and large-scale deployment management</li> <li>Platform Administration: High availability, disaster recovery, cluster orchestration, observability and audit (e.g. Amazon CloudWatch / CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Google Cloud Operations Suite), and cloud cost management</li> <li>Infrastructure Automation (InfraOps): Hands-on automation using IaC tools (e.g. Terraform, plus cloud-native tooling such as AWS CloudFormation / CDK, Azure Resource Manager / Bicep, or Google Cloud Deployment Manager) to build, maintain, and scale complex cloud environments</li> </ul> <li>Solid grounding in distributed data systems architecture: scalable pipelines, streaming architectures, lakehouse patterns, and cloud-native data platforms</li> <li>Proficient on the Databricks Platform (or demonstrated ability to achieve proficiency rapidly) with a developing technical specialisation in one area (e.g. real-time/streaming, ML/AI, data governance, migrations)</li> <li>Ability to contribute to architecture discussions with senior technical stakeholders (including CISOs and risk/compliance stakeholders): whiteboarding, design reviews, and trade-off analysis. Own complex, cross-functional security engagements end to end.</li> <li>Track record unblocking adoption of new features (AI, serverless) by clearing security and compliance blockers within accounts.</li> <li>Contribute to Field Engineering thought leadership through customer-facing content, workshops, and community engagement</li> <li>Excellent communication skills: able to translate complex architectures into business value for both technical and executive audiences</li> <li>Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a quantitative discipline (or equivalent experience)</li> <li>Willingness to travel up to 30% as needed</li> </ul> <p> </p> <p><strong>Nice to Have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Databricks certifications (Data Engineer, ML, Platform)</li> <li>Cloud provider certifications at professional level (e.g. AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional or AWS Certified Data Engineer; Azure Solutions Architect Expert; Google Professional Cloud Architect)</li> <li>Experience with competitive platforms (Snowflake, cloud-native data services, Azure Synapse, BigQuery), understanding the landscape you'll position against</li> <li>Background in a data/AI company or cloud provider</li> </ul> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>About Databricks</strong></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, sans-serif;">Databricks is the Data and AI company. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. title: Senior Identity Security Engineer
description: <p><strong>Scopely </strong>is looking for a <strong>Senior Identity Security Engineer</strong> to join our Information Security team on a remote basis or hybrid basis if located in Barcelona.  This is a hands-on engineer who will build identity controls that reduce excessive privilege and protect critical operations. You will improve access across employee, player, business partner, and non-human identities by building AI-native identity workflows: agentic systems that handle provisioning, access reviews, and remediation within explicit guardrails, with humans approving what matters. Your work will protect the identities and access that support Scopely’s critical business processes, including essential enterprise functions and game operations.  This is a highly technical, hands-on role for someone who can operate across AWS, GCP, Okta, AWS IAM Identity Center, Zero Trust access models, identity governance workflows, and modern AI-enabled engineering environments, while building scalable identity systems through Infrastructure as Code, workflow orchestration, and automation-first security engineering.</p> <p><strong>What You Will Do</strong></p> <p><strong>Reduce identity attack surface and privilege</strong></p> <ul> <li>Reduce standing and excessive access with least-privilege roles, just-in-time and time-bound elevation, and automated access reviews.</li> <li>Build repeatable identity and access workflows that make onboarding, approvals, role changes, reviews, and offboarding consistent, traceable, and timely.</li> <li>Govern non-human identities, including service accounts, workload identities, CI/CD identities, API credentials, and AI agents and their tool integrations: inventory them, assign owners, replace long-lived secrets with short-lived or federated credentials, and rotate or revoke on a schedule and on signal.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Strengthen identity protection and resilience</strong></p> <ul> <li>Protect access to critical business processes and systems with phishing-resistant authentication (passkeys/FIDO2), device trust and posture signals, tightly controlled privileged access, and prompt revocation of suspicious sessions or compromised credentials.</li> <li>Threat-model identity platforms, integrations, and access paths to identify exploitable trust relationships, privilege escalation, and credential misuse. </li> <li>Build identity telemetry and response workflows to detect risky sign-ins, privilege changes, credential misuse, and compromised integrations. </li> <li>Design and test break-glass and recovery procedures for identity services and cloud access so teams can regain secure access during an outage or compromise.</li> <li>Extend the same patterns to player and partner identities where security owns the controls: platform identity federation (Apple, Google, Steam, console), account linking and recovery, external and vendor access, and defenses against account takeover and credential stuffing.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Build AI-native identity services</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build and operate reusable identity controls and services using infrastructure as code, APIs, scripting, and delivery pipelines. Apply code review, testing, drift detection, and audit trails so that every change, whether made by an engineer or an agent, is safe to deploy and easy to investigate.</li> <li>Design and build multi-agent workflows that surface identity risk, run access attestations, and triage and remediate access issues end to end. Engineer the harness those agents run in: scoped tools and permissions, curated context and data access, evals and test cases, orchestration between agents, and observability, so agent behavior is predictable, reviewable, and improvable.</li> <li>Treat agents as identities. Give every agent and MCP integration its own scoped credentials, least-privilege permissions, and bounded data access; validate inputs and outputs; log every action; and require human approval for changes that touch privileged access or production.</li> <li>Work with game and platform stakeholders to adopt shared identity patterns. Measure progress through reduced standing privilege, stale access, and unmanaged identities, and less manual work.</li> <li>Produce audit-ready evidence for access reviews, privileged access, and lifecycle events as a byproduct of the workflows rather than a separate project.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of experience in IAM, or identity-focused cloud/security engineering, including hands-on ownership of production identity controls in complex environments.</li> <li>Strong experience with Okta or a comparable workforce identity platform and AWS/GCP IAM, as well as federation and provisioning protocols such as SAML, OIDC, OAuth, and SCIM.</li> <li>Production experience building, testing, and operating identity services or automation using Terraform or comparable infrastructure as code, Python, Go, or TypeScript., APIs, version control, and CI/CD.</li> <li>Strong knowledge of least privilege, just-in-time privileged access, identity lifecycle and governance, authentication controls, and non-human or workload identity risk.</li> <li>Experience threat-modeling identity architectures, integrations, and access paths, and driving remediation with service owners.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building AI-native workflows: systems where agents carry out multi-step work end to end, designed from the start around what agents can be trusted to do and where humans approve. Using a coding assistant does not count.</li> <li>Working fluency with harness engineering and multi-agent development: defining tools and permissions, scoping context and data, writing evals, orchestrating specialized agents, and instrumenting agent runs so failures are diagnosable, plus the judgment to keep those systems inside least-privilege boundaries.</li> <li>Ability to lead technical work from design through deployment and operations, and explain identity risks and implementation choices to stakeholders.</li> <li>Experience with identity governance, privileged access, or cloud entitlement tooling, or having built the equivalent in-house.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice-to-have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Consumer identity (CIAM) at scale, Kubernetes workload identity, detection engineering or SIEM experience, Okta or cloud security certifications, gaming or live-service experience.</li> </ul> <p><strong><br><br></strong></p><div class="content-conclusion"><p> </p> <h3>About Scopely</h3> <p>Scopely is a leading video game and global interactive entertainment company, home to many of the world’s most beloved and enduring experiences, including two of the most successful mobile games of all-time “MONOPOLY GO!” and “Pokémon GO,” along with “Stumble Guys,” “Star Trek™ Fleet Command,” “MARVEL Strike Force,” “WWE Champions,” the Scrabble® franchise, “Yahtzee® With Buddies,” and many others. Across mobile, web, PC, and console, Scopely creates, develops, publishes, and live-operates one of the most diversified and award-winning portfolios in the games industry — bringing hundreds of millions of players together through a shared love of play.</p> <p>Founded in 2011, Scopely is powered by its exceptional team — including thousands of world-class gamemakers around the globe, a distinctive tenet-driven culture, and its proprietary technology platform, Playgami. Together, these strengths have fueled Scopely’s position as the #1 mobile games company in the U.S. and #2 globally, generating more than $10 billion in lifetime revenue. Whether building global sensations like “MONOPOLY GO!” from the ground up, or expanding through strategic acquisitions, including the FoxNext, GSN, and Scopely Explore games businesses — Scopely consistently delivers experiences players love today and return to for years to come.</p> <p>Recognized multiple times as one of the "100 Most Influential Companies in the World" by TIME magazine and one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies" and “Best Workplaces for Innovators,” Scopely believes that video games can be a force for good — creating meaningful connections, vibrant communities, and making life better through play.</p> <p>Scopely has global operations and partners across four continents in more than a dozen countries worldwide. For more information, visit: <a href="https://www.scopely.com/">https://www.scopely.com/</a>. </p> <p>Notice to Candidates: Scopely will never request payment or financial information during the application or hiring process. Please apply only through our official <a href="http://scopely.com">website</a> and verify that all Talent Partner communications come from an email address ending in @<a href="http://scopely.com">scopely.com</a>.</p> <p>Should you have any questions or encounter any fraudulent requests/emails/websites, please immediately contact ----- Our job applicant privacy policies are available here: <a href="https://www.scopely.com/en/job-applicant-privacy-notice-for-ca-residents">California Privacy Notice</a> and <a href="https://www.scopely.com/en/eea-and-uk-job-applicant-privacy-notice">EEA/UK Privacy Notice</a>.</p> <p>Employment at Scopely is based solely on a person's merit and qualifications. Scopely does not discriminate against any employee or applicant because of race, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding), or any other basis protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.</p> <p>For more information, visit <a href="wppmedia.com">wppmedia.com</a>.</p></div><p></p> <p><strong>3623 - Director, Planning - UK</strong></p> <p><strong>Role Summary and Impact</strong></p> <p>We are recruiting for a Business Director who is an exceptional and driven media planner, to join our Connections Planning team working on the Ford account.</p> <p>We work in a unique ‘full service’ model meaning that the media teams collaborate closely with creative and account management teams within the Ford agency structure (primarily working with VML and WPP Production).</p> <p>Therefore we foster a fully integrated team approach across media, creative and client, working together across the agency and client locations - Ford’s Dunton office (a short taxi from Shenfield on the Elizabeth Line - travel costs are covered) when required, balanced with working together in WPP Rose Court London with creative and social teams.</p> <p>Your role, as a Business Director, will report to the Planning Lead, with support from the EVP, Clients, and will be focused on leading a team to deliver the planning and account management for Ford of Britain, across both Personal Vehicles and Commercial Vehicles. You will get the opportunity to design exciting, award-winning campaigns as well as work with channel specialists to make those plans a reality. Mindshare work on the Ford account globally, and whilst this role is UK specific there is a lot of collaboration between the teams.</p> <p>The remit also includes working in an integrated team leading on ESOP planning (earned, shared, owned and paid), collaborating closely with the creative team (VML) as well as the social team (WPP Production).</p> <p>You will be expected to demonstrate experience and knowledge in:</p> <ul> <li>Excellent stakeholder management with both clients and agency alike</li> <li>Ability to work with clients to ensure the brief is right with clear and measurable objectives in place</li> <li>An ability to think and work ‘audience first’, translating audience insight into actionable audiences </li> <li>Specify how to build and target audiences in addressable and non-addressable media and validate the approach to ensure that the defined audience can be reached at the scale required</li> <li>Designing an approach that outlines how and where we will connect with defined audiences in media</li> <li>Leading ESOP planning (earned, shared, owned and paid) within an integrated team</li> <li>Designing the connections ecosystem & plan, working closely and collaboratively with channel specialists </li> <li>Day to day management of campaigns as a key liaison between clients and channel specialists </li> <li>Designing measurement & testing framework to inform as well as measure and optimise the campaigns</li> <li>Line management of planning team within account structure</li> <li>Responsibilities to the planning department as senior member of the team, contributing to Business Director board meetings and leading work streams. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong></p> <p>At WPP Media, we believe in the power of our culture and our people. tangibly prove your plans are aimed at achieving excellence in planning craft.</li> <li>You can create a holistic measurement framework that is relevant for the brand and every campaign (setting KPIs, methods i.e., which tool/system, necessary tracking) and plans for adaptation/optimisation).  </li> <li>You must have extensive experience leading senior client relationships, managing all agency teams, leading and delivering client projects and tackling challenging conversations.</li> <li>You are an excellent team player taking the responsibility for working in a collaborative, inclusive way to allow specialists to contribute.</li> <li>You demonstrate a high degree of organisation that leads to successfully managing workflow for self and more junior members of the team.</li> <li>You are open-minded, flexible and embracing of agile ways of working.</li> </ul> <p><strong>The Ideal Candidate</strong></p> <p>As Business Director you will be responsible for the leadership and delivery of best-in-class planning and implementation. </p> <ul> <li>You will have a strong desire to deliver innovative and effective work both reactively (in response to briefs), and proactively (spotting those opportunities for insight and innovation outside of briefs). </li> <li>We expect our Business Directors to show a breath of understanding of media channels, as well as in-depth and speciality understanding in how to discuss the present and future role each channel plays as part of a comms strategy. </li> <li>Strong people management skills.</li> <li>Collaborative both in the day-to-day account role and across the planning department.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Life at WPP Media & Benefits</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media includes investing in our employees to help them do their best work, and we’re just as committed to employee growth as we are to responsible media investment. description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. About Deliveroo Our mission is to transform the way people shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of one of the most rapidly expanding industries in the world: a complex, always-on, three-sided marketplace that impacts millions of people every day. Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. The Team BizOps is the team that keeps its finger on the pulse of business performance: continuously, rigorously, and across multiple dimensions at once. We turn raw operational and financial data into actionable intelligence, surfacing what is happening, why it is happening, and what to expect next , for the operators, executives, and functional teams who run the business day to day. We are not a reporting function that produces outputs on request. We work continuously, proactively watching, delivering, and questioning whether the signal is real, acting as "first responders" to surprising deviations from expectation and using what we learn to drive faster, better decision-making for the business at large. Our work spans the full stack of analytics: from the warehouse models that make metrics trustworthy, to the monitoring systems that catch problems early, to the reports and dashboards that make performance visible, to the deep-dive investigations that explain what the numbers mean and what we should do about it. We anchor our analysis to the right reference points: how performance compares to plan, to prior periods, and to what we'd expect, and we bring causal rigour when the business needs to know whether an action actually worked. The culture within the team is informal, fast-paced and entrepreneurial. Given the growth of the business and the level of senior stakeholder exposure, progression in the team can be fast. The Role Deliveroo is hiring a Senior Data Scientist to join BizOps, based in our London HQ (hybrid, minimum three days per week in the office). This role is largely project-based: starting from a strategic or performance question, you'll combine data, business context, and structured problem-solving to provide the insights that drive decision-making at a global level with senior stakeholders. You will own delivery end-to-end, from the messy, ambiguous question to a rigorous, trustworthy, and actionable answer. You'll be equally comfortable building the systems that make performance visible and going deep on the investigations that explain it. One week you might diagnose why a key market has moved away from plan; the next, identify the drivers behind a change in customer or operational performance; the next, build monitoring that helps teams spot and understand emerging issues earlier. Success in this role requires building effective working relationships across Deliveroo, particularly with international markets, as well as the Data Science, Operations, Commercial, and Finance teams. Deconstruct broad, ambiguous problem spaces into structured analytical roadmaps, and understand how your work intersects with adjacent systems and teams. Build for scale, not one-offs. Build the pipelines, models, dashboards, monitoring, and investigative tooling that make performance visible and reliable. Automate wherever possible; redoing analyses by hand is slow and error-prone. Measure impact with discipline. Design measurement strategies from simple A/B tests to quasi-experimental designs (synthetic control, difference-in-differences, event studies) when trials aren't feasible, always with conservative, assumption-explicit language. Proficiency with SQL and a scripting language such as Python or R, alongside experience with BI or visualisation tooling such as Looker, Tableau, or similar. Comfortable using modern AI-assisted tools to work efficiently while maintaining high standards of accuracy and reproducibility. A pragmatic approach to problem-solving: you can balance analytical rigour with speed, adapt your approach to the importance of the decision, and focus effort where it will have the greatest impact. Effective problem-solving: you can take an ambiguous question, identify the underlying problem or decision, develop hypotheses, and use data and business context to reach a clear point of view. Experience with experimentation and/or causal inference is a strong plus: the ability to unpick insights and steer strategic decisions. Excellent communication skills, in person, in writing, and in code, with the ability to translate business needs into analytical problems and complex findings into simple recommendations. Driven, hard-working, and agile. BizOps sits at the centre of a fast-growing business; we move quickly to scale at pace. London-based, with a minimum of three days per week in the office. Why Join Us? title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer GAIA
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our Simulation Teams You'll be joining the Simulation team (Simulation Evaluation & Validation), working on Gaia — Wayve's world model. Gaia is trained on large-scale driving video to predict future frames from past context, functioning as a simulator that generates synthetic scenarios and operates in closed loop with the driving model itself. The team partners closely with Research, Applications, Core Simulation Engineering, and Cloud/Infrastructure to turn model improvements into measurable downstream impact on the driving stack. 🧠 Your day-to-day Own and lead parts of large-scale training for Gaia (language- or video-style training at scale), from experimentation through productionised training runs. Contribute to and influence model architecture decisions — not just applying existing models. Partner across sub-teams: Research (model development), Applications (adapting models to use cases), Core Simulation Engineering, and Cloud/Infrastructure. Translate product and evaluation needs into model improvements (e.g. better long-horizon prediction, scenario generation quality, failure-case coverage). Mentor and set technical direction, raising the engineering and research quality bar across the team. 🧩 What you’ll be working on Leading and executing Gaia's post-training and closed-loop pipeline — fine-tuning and aligning the world model through post-training experimentation and targeted data curation. Pushing Gaia's autoregressive generation towards longer, more stable rollouts, and making the model deployment-ready (inference time and reliability included). Contributing to broader model architecture and training-strategy decisions where they intersect with pre- and post-training and the application layer. Partnering closely with research, applications, simulation engineering, and cloud/infrastructure teams to translate post-training improvements into measurable downstream impact. Providing technical leadership through mentorship, review, and setting high engineering/research standards. 🙌 You should apply if Essential: You have hands-on experience post-training/fine-tuning large-scale models (language, video, or other foundation models). You have experience with world models, autoregressive generation, and long-horizon generation. You have experience with diffusion/flow models and a solid understanding of 3D vision. You have a strong understanding of model architecture and can contribute meaningfully to architectural/training decisions. You have strong hands-on engineering skills with modern ML stacks (e.g. PyTorch), including debugging and performance/reliability-minded development. You have 5+ years of relevant industry experience (advanced degrees are valued, but depth of applied experience matters more). Desirable: Experience with inference optimisation or deploying large models under latency/compute constraints. Experience improving data/training pipelines and working across infrastructure constraints (distributed training, efficiency, reliability). Proven technical leadership — tech lead ownership, mentoring, or setting direction across an area. 🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 🔍 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) Competency Interviews (Programming/Pytorch debugging and hiring manager interview; 2 hours total) Deep-dive technical interviews (Systems & domain-specific interviews; 3 hours total) Final interview : Mission & values alignment (45 mins). We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability. What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more A quick, honest note before you apply. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. VML, part of WPP, supports WPP Enterprise Solutions by helping brands activate transformation through creativity and experience.</p></div><h3>Senior Consultant with experience in Commerce ecosystems and technologies wanted to join our Business Services team </h3> <h3>The opportunity:</h3> <p>How consumers discover, evaluate and buy products is changing faster than most organisations can respond. AI-powered search, agentic commerce, generative product discovery and the collapse of the traditional funnel are reshaping commercial models across every sector. Most enterprise clients know something has shifted, few have a clear plan for what to do about it.</p> <p>WPP Enterprise Solutions is building a commerce consulting practice to help clients navigate these shifts. What makes this role different from a boutique or a SaaS provider is what sits around you: your consulting recommendations connect directly to creative, content, CX and commerce execution teams who bring them to life. Strategy doesn't end at a slide deck here.</p> <p>We're looking for a Senior Consultant who can own projects and client relationships. Someone who takes an ambiguous brief, structures it independently, drives the strategic direction and ensures the quality of everything the team delivers. You'll lead client conversations, design and facilitate workshops, and be the person mid-to-senior client stakeholders trust to connect diagnostic findings to commercial action. You'll also play a key role in growing the practice, spotting extension opportunities within accounts, contributing to pitches and coaching more junior members of the team.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Perm </strong></li> <li><strong>London/Hybrid </strong></li> <li><strong>Travel to client site where required</strong></li> </ul> <h3>What you’ll be doing:</h3> <p><em><strong>Project Leadership & Delivery</strong></em></p> <ul> <li>Own medium-scale projects end-to-end: scope, quality, delivery timeline, and client relationship. Accountable for the strategic direction and the standard of output.</li> <li>Lead the development of strategic recommendations across commerce transformation, AI discoverability (GEO/AEO), agentic commerce readiness, content strategy and channel optimisation - shaping the narrative, not just building the analysis.</li> <li>Take ambiguous or loosely defined briefs and structure them into clear project plans with defined deliverables, milestones and resource requirements.</li> <li>Build and codify delivery methodologies into repeatable, scalable frameworks the wider team can execute against.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Client Leadership:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Design and lead workshops, stakeholder interviews and co-creation sessions. You will be comfortable going off-script when the conversation requires it and steering senior client stakeholders toward actionable outcomes.</li> <li>Serve as a trusted advisor to mid-to-senior client contacts. You are the person they call when they need the thinking sharpened or the direction challenged.<br>Anticipate and respond to client questions in a compelling and informed way. Own the client relationship day-to-day, identifying when senior escalation or support is needed.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Business Development:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify growth opportunities within existing accounts - spot the extension, the adjacent brief, the unasked question and work with senior leadership to convert them.</li> <li>Contribute meaningfully to proposals and pitch responses: shaping the strategic approach, writing key sections, and presenting to prospective clients where appropriate.</li> <li>Build client relationships that generate repeat work - not just deliver well, but leave clients wanting more.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team & Practice Building:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Coach and develop Consultants on the team: Setting the quality bar on projects, giving direct feedback, and creating opportunities for junior team members to stretch.</li> <li>This role may line-manage 1–2 team members, depending on team structure.</li> <li>Drive practice IP development: reusable frameworks, case studies, proposition collateral and points of view that strengthen our market position and make selling easier.</li> <li>Work across WPP's integrated network: connecting upstream consulting recommendations to downstream execution in content, CX and commerce.</li> </ul> <h3>What we want from you:</h3> <ul> <li>Extensive professional experience, with a strong track record in consulting, strategy or senior commercial/digital roles (ideally blending both)</li> <li>Deep understanding of how commerce ecosystems work: You've either run a commerce operation (brand-side) or advised on one (agency/consulting-side). You understand how trading, content, category management, channel strategy and technology intersect in practice.</li> <li>Working knowledge of AI discoverability: GEO, AEO, LLM-influenced discovery, AI assistants and conversational commerce. You can advise a Head of Digital or VP of eCommerce on what this shift means for their business and back it up with a credible action plan.</li> <li>Proven ability to lead projects independently - you've managed scope, quality and client expectations without someone looking over your shoulder.</li> <li>Strong strategic and analytical thinking: you can take a diagnostic output or a data-heavy assessment and turn it into a clear, commercially prioritised set of recommendations with a compelling narrative.</li> <li>Excellent communication and executive presence - you're comfortable leading a room, running a workshop, and navigating a difficult client conversation with credibility.</li> <li>Experience building methodology or practice IP: You've created frameworks, playbooks or delivery approaches that others have adopted and scaled.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Ideally you will have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Brand-side experience in eCommerce, digital marketing or commercial leadership - you've lived the reality of managing a P&L, running a digital operation, or leading a commerce team. This perspective is what separates a genuine consultant from a presenter of slides.</li> <li>Experience in at least two of: CPG/FMCG, Consumer health, Automotive, Retail, Telecom.</li> <li>Change management or enablement experience: you've helped organisations adopt new operating models, not just designed them.</li> <li>Line management or mentoring experience.</li> </ul> <p><strong>If you know some of this, even better:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Hands-on curiosity with AI tools LLMs, agentic platforms, or similar.</li> <li>Experience with commerce technology (Shopify, SFCC, Commercetools, PIM/DAM systems).</li> </ul> <h3>What we can offer you:</h3> <ul> <li>The chance to shape a growing consulting practice your work will define methodology and propositions, not just execute someone else's.</li> <li>Direct access to iconic enterprise clients and the opportunity to contribute to both proposition development and project delivery.</li> <li>An integrated agency network where your title: Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer
description: ABOUT US At Heim, we are reinventing how healthcare is delivered. We believe that healthcare is best delivered in the home of patients, and that we are at the cusp of a systemic shift away from hospital based care. Our mission is to expand access to in-person clinical care at home by empowering community nurses with technology that makes care delivery more efficient. We have created an AI native ecosystem that optimises the complex scheduling involved in delivering community based care, and are on track to automate every non clinical touchpoint for nurses. To date, our technology has powered our network of 400+ practitioners to deliver c. 30K appointments, and we have shown that our algorithms bring down the cost of at-home visits by c.35% whilst freeing up valuable time for care in doing so. We are growing fast and our ambitions are big – with new international markets on the roadmap, and strong investor backing. Our aim is to create the most productive, AI-enabled distributed clinical workforce working at the intersection of public and private health.By joining Heim, you will play a pivotal role in building the infrastructure that puts clinical care in the home. WHAT IT'S LIKE TO WORK AT HEIM We are reinventing how healthcare is delivered. Here are the things that shape your day-to-day: Meaningful problems – we build systems that improve how organisations understand and care for people. The work is complex, applied, and grounded in real-world patient impact High standards, low ego – you’ll work alongside thoughtful engineers, clinicians, and operators who care about clarity and good judgement Speed with intent – we move quickly but deliberately. Clear ownership, evidence-based decisions, outcomes over output Simple, elegant solutions – we have a strong bias towards code that is easy to reason about, hard to break, and built to outlast the sprint it was born in Direct access to founders – you’ll have visibility into and input on the direction of the company WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DIFFERENT This is a full-stack TypeScript role in the truest sense – you will own problems across the entire system, from UI to infrastructure. AI isn’t a feature here; it’s a first principle. We expect you to use agentic coding tools fluently (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) and to be building your own views on where agentic workflows can meaningfully improve what we ship. You’ll be working on systems where the stakes are real: scheduling errors affect patient care, data quality issues affect clinical decisions, and downtime has consequences. That context sharpens every technical choice you make. WHAT YOU'LL DO Design and build product features end-to-end across the Heim tech stack – owning them from first principles to production Architect and implement AI-powered workflows: scheduling optimisation, practitioner dispatch, clinical data enrichment, and agentic referral automations that reduce manual touchpoints for nurses Own the full lifecycle of features – from TypeScript frontend through to backend services, infrastructure, deployment pipelines, and testing – without relying on separate DevOps or QA teams to close the loop Build and maintain the APIs, services, and data models that underpin clinical operations – with the reliability and auditability a regulated environment demands Collaborate with our product and clinical ops teams to translate ambiguous real-world problems into working software Make pragmatic trade-offs between speed and quality, and advocate clearly when the trade-off isn’t acceptable Contribute to the architecture and infrastructure decisions that will shape the platform as we scale to NHS Trusts across the UK and into new markets Leave the codebase better than you found it – improving performance, clarity, and resilience as part of everyday delivery You won’t get perfectly specified tickets. You’ll be trusted to think, decide, and ship. HOW WE WORK Small team, fast loops, few layers – your decisions land fast and the feedback is real We operate a hybrid team set up, and value high quality in person time so you must be able to commute to our central London office Technical judgement is respected and expected – you’ll have a real voice in architectural decisions Disagreement is normal. Good ideas win, not hierarchical ones Strong bias toward execution: fewer meetings, clear ownership, and decisions grounded in evidence WHO THIS IS FOR You’re a senior full-stack engineer who acts like a founder. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks. You’re comfortable roaming an unfamiliar part of the codebase when something needs fixing, and you’ll ask sharp clarifying questions before committing to an approach. You probably have: 6+ years building and owning production software in fast-moving environments Genuine full-stack capability – you’re not “mostly frontend” or “mostly backend”; you care about and can own the whole system Proven ability to own the full delivery lifecycle: frontend, backend, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, deployment, and testing – without handing off to separate DevOps or QA teams Active, fluent use of AI coding tools – Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot – not as novelty, but as default workflow Experience making data-sensitive engineering decisions: you instinctively ask about PII classification, schema flexibility, and audit requirements before you build A track record of shipping under ambiguity – you’ve taken a vague ask, formed a point of view, and delivered something that worked The judgement to know when to move fast and when to slow down Bonus if you have: Experience in regulated environments (healthcare, fintech, legal) and an understanding of what “good enough” looks like when data sensitivity is high Background building agentic or multi-step AI workflows in production A side project or personal tool built with AI – something that shows you’ve been hands-on with Cursor, Claude Code, or AI integrations outside of work Familiarity with NHS data standards, FHIR, or community care systems Infrastructure and cloud experience (GCP or equivalent) beyond the basics Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: About GetGround GetGround is the all-in-one platform for UK property investors, helping landlords find, finance, structure and manage buy-to-let investments, and prepare and file their tax returns. Investors around the world trust us with their companies, finances and property. Purpose of the role You will assist with the design and running of GetGround's data privacy and AI governance programmes day to day, working closely with the Senior Director - Legal, Risk & Compliance. You will advise teams, keep our compliance records current, handle rights requests and breaches, and build our AI governance framework so that the AI tools we use are lawful and well controlled. Data privacy responsibilities Advise teams on their obligations under the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, PECR and the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025. Run the data privacy compliance programme to the DPO's assurance plan, covering policies, records of processing, retention, training and audits. Support business owners to complete DPIAs and keep the DPIA register. Deliver the data protection framework for Self Assessment and Making Tax Digital processing Review data-sharing, processor and partner agreements, including white-label partnerships, and international transfer arrangements. Handle subject access and other rights requests and data privacy complaints; prepare breach assessments with Information Security for the DPO's decision. Prepare data privacy evidence for partner due diligence. Deliver data privacy training and keep the Senior Director and business up to date on legal and regulatory changes AI governance responsibilities Build and maintain a register of AI systems and use cases, including third-party tools, with an owner and risk rating for each. Run risk assessments for new AI use cases, combined with DPIAs where personal data is involved, covering accuracy, bias, transparency and human oversight. Maintain the Responsible Use of AI Policy and governance framework, and deliver AI training. Advise on safeguards for automated decision-making, including the right to human review. Review AI vendors and model providers before onboarding, and keep a log of AI incidents, tracking each to closure. Prepare reports to the Risk & Compliance Committee on data privacy and AI governance. In addition to the above, the role will involve contributing to a number of strategic growth projects across the business and collaborating closely with other members of the Legal, Risk & Compliance team to build a scalable and comprehensive approach to managing data privacy and AI risk, enabling proper governance, oversight and streamlined legal, risk and compliance processes. Skills and experience Essential Expert, current knowledge of UK data protection law and ICO guidance. Working knowledge of AI governance, including ICO guidance on AI and data protection, the EU AI Act, and frameworks such as ISO/IEC 42001 or the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. At least five years in a data privacy role in a company, such as data protection manager or privacy lead, with experience of governing AI or automated decision-making. Experience in financial services, fintech, proptech or another regulated, data-heavy business. Track record of running DPIAs and AI risk assessments, handling incidents and managing rights requests at volume. Ability to turn legal requirements into practical, commercial advice, and the confidence to challenge and execute on tasks within tight timeframes Desirable IAPP CIPP/E or CIPM, or the BCS Practitioner Certificate in Data Protection; IAPP AIGP; a legal qualification. Experience of data protection in tax, accountancy or HMRC agent services, including Making Tax Digital. Knowledge of AML/KYC processes, FCA expectations and EU, Hong Kong or Singapore data protection rules. What we are building: The first end-to-end real estate investment offering - making the dream of owning real estate more accessible to everyone globally. description: About Us: Fireworks is the platform for specialized intelligence, enabling companies to build, train, and serve AI models tailored to their own data, workflows, and products. Founded by the team behind PyTorch and backed by AMD, Atreides, Benchmark Capital, Index Ventures, Lightspeed, NVIDIA, Sequoia Capital, and TCV, Fireworks powers production AI with hundreds of state-of-the-art open models across text, image, embedding, audio, and multimodal workloads. Today, Fireworks is a Series D company valued at $17.5 billion, bringing together an ambitious, collaborative team that's building the future of enterprise AI. The Role: As an Applied Machine Learning Engineer, you are the technical owner of a customer engagement. This is what is globally known as the Forward Deployed Engineer role; at Fireworks in EMEA it carries the AMLE title. You embed with a small number of accounts, work in their environment, and own whatever stands between them and production on Fireworks: the model, the serving path, the integration, the performance. You scope the work before signature and deliver what you scoped. Depth over breadth: few accounts, owned end to end. What we value most is first principles thinking: reasoning about unfamiliar problems from the ground up rather than from playbooks. You will be evaluated on this directly in the interview process, and strength here can outweigh gaps elsewhere in your background. Four Spikes: Software engineering. You ship production systems and are comfortable dropped into an unfamiliar codebase or a customer environment with a deadline. Backend and systems depth, strong Python plus at least one systems language, and fluency with AI-assisted and agentic engineering as a core part of how you build. Machine learning. You take open models and make them better on a customer's task: SFT, LoRA and other parameter-efficient methods, reinforcement learning (RLHF, RLVR), distillation. Just as important, you design evaluations that reflect the real task and let them drive training decisions, and you know when fine-tuning is not the answer. Infrastructure and performance. You know your GPUs: memory bandwidth, kernels, parallelism, what utilization numbers actually mean. Serving and inference optimization: quantization, speculative decoding, batching, KV cache behavior, latency vs throughput tradeoffs, multi-GPU and multi-node serving, capacity planning. You can take a deployment that works and make it fast and economical, and reason about where the bottleneck is before touching a profiler. Customer engagement. You want to be in the room. The point of this role is creating specialized intelligence for each customer: the best model for their task, their data, their constraints. That takes real interest in the customer's problem, not just the technical one. Exceptional here looks like founder energy with customers; the floor is genuine appetite to embed, explain, and own outcomes with them. Key Responsibilities: Own Engagements: Take customer deployments from scoping through production, as the single accountable technical owner. Embed: Work directly inside customer teams; understand their domain, data, and constraints well enough to make decisions they trust. Train and Tune: Run fine-tuning and post-training work where the engagement needs it, from data to evaluation to a model serving in production. Optimize: Drive serving performance and cost on Fireworks: model choice, deployment shape, and inference optimization. Scope Honestly: Assess what is achievable before we commit, and inherit what you scope. Product Signal: Feed what customers need back to product and engineering, with enough precision to be actionable. Minimum Qualifications: Spikes in two or all three areas. For the ML spike: formal training (PhD, PhD in progress, or a strong MSc) and experience post-training LLMs specifically. For the infrastructure spike: experience with GPU infrastructure, distributed serving, or inference engines. Founder or founding engineer experience. Experience in a startup or fast-paced environment. Why Fireworks? Solve Hard Problems: Tackle challenges at the forefront of AI infrastructure, from low-latency inference to scalable model serving. Build What’s Next: Work with bleeding-edge technology that impacts how businesses and developers harness AI globally. Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of AI—no bureaucracy, just results. Learn from the Best: Collaborate with world-class engineers and AI researchers who thrive on curiosity and innovation. Fireworks AI is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all innovators. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month. You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works. As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today. It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on. The machine that builds the product We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right. I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job. That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster. Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents. You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients. What you'll do Build the machine that builds the product Most of your time goes here. Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure. Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write. Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering. Own the platform Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model. Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect. Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team. Work across the stack Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from. Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on. Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person. Your first six months Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality. At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients. Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients. Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in. Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on. How you'll work You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them. You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong. This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work. You'll probably enjoy this if You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one. You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it. You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team. You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster. You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week. You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so. This probably isn't for you if You want a pure DevOps or SRE role. You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible. What you'll bring Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you. Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda. Infrastructure as code as a habit , with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code. Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt. Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's. Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb. Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do. Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple. Tooling you've built for AI agents , not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review. Our stack TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.
